question: Graded by KiCad under each board's own rules with one grader (tools/kicad-oracle of the q22 commit), does main after Q22 (the q22 commit, with Q22.16, Q22.17 and Q22.18 in) route the 14 rows through the plugin's export with the plugin's default options and zero routing-caused manufacturing breaches on every row, and what did Q22 cost or save in KiCad unconnected items against main a8b4ae7, the last main before any Q22 routing or plugin fix?
rule_text: Decided 2026-10-20: Q22's fixes are correctness fixes, already landed, so there is no profile promotion and no keep decision. The verdict is the guard alone (keep_rule). The gate's paired improve/regress verdict on kicad_unconnected is printed and not used
engine: two release builds of freerouting-cli, one per arm (arms.*.engine); Q22.8's first amendment, written after both builds and before any route, names the q22 commit, both binaries' sha256 and `freerouting-rs --version`, the sha256 of the q22 commit's tools/kicad-oracle/{grade.sh,oracle_lib.py,kicad_steps.py,via_in_pad.py} and of each tree's kicad-plugin/headless_run.py, and options.SCHEMA at the q22 commit

steps: rm -rf Q/before-tree/tools/kicad-oracle && git -C /home/thebo/code/freerouting-rs archive Q22_COMMIT tools/kicad-oracle | tar -x -C Q/before-tree
check: `diff -r Q/before-tree/tools/kicad-oracle Q/q22-tree/tools/kicad-oracle` prints nothing; `git -C Q/before-tree diff --quiet a8b4ae7 -- kicad-plugin crates Cargo.toml Cargo.lock` exits 0
in each tree: CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_TARGET_DIR=Q/target-ARM cargo build --release -p freerouting-cli (one build at a time)
trees.how_the_arm_picks_its_plugin: grade.sh sets HERE to its own directory and runs HEADLESS=$HERE/../../kicad-plugin/headless_run.py for --export plugin (export and import). Run from Q/before-tree, the q22 commit's grade.sh therefore exports and imports with a8b4ae7's headless_run.py and its freerouting_rs modules, while LIB (oracle_lib.py) and STEPS (kicad_steps.py: version, strip, stats) are the q22 commit's. kicad_steps.py reads kicad-plugin/freerouting_rs (PLUGIN_MODULES) only in its own `import`, which grade.sh runs for the bare export only, never with --export plugin. via_in_pad.py imports only pcbnew. Q22.8's first amendment checks with `grep -n kicad-plugin Q/q22-tree/tools/kicad-oracle/*.sh Q/q22-tree/tools/kicad-oracle/*.py` that the q22 grader still reads nothing else of kicad-plugin/, or says what it reads
trees.how_the_arm_picks_its_engine: the engine command names the arm's binary by absolute path (Q/target-ARM/release/freerouting-rs); grade.sh runs it from OUT/work. FREEROUTING_DEV=/nonexistent turns off grade.sh's optional tidiness step (Q15.2) in both arms, so neither arm reads a freerouting-dev

command_placeholders.BOARD: the main checkout's root joined with the row's `input` (absolute; grade.sh takes the .kicad_pcb itself and reads its .kicad_pro/.kicad_dru beside it)

options.default_why: the plugin's defaults: options.profile_defaults('enhanced').to_dict() is {"schema": 5, "profile": "enhanced"} at registration (main 5926b61), and a8b4ae7's options.READABLE_SCHEMAS is (1, 2, 3, 4, 5), so a8b4ae7's plugin reads the same file. The Board Setup minimums are not options: each arm's plugin reads them from the board (export_flow.router_args), which is why the arms' flags differ by Q22.10's and Q22.11's minimums and Q22.5's --kicad-dru

boards.why: Paths are relative to the main checkout's root, under target/ (not in git); the copies were made 2026-10-20 into target/orchestrator/q227/boards/, and a missing copy is re-made from the row's source and must hash as registered. The twelve rows from N04.3 hash as docs/roadmap/prereg/N04.json's `boards.files`. keep_tracks: the N04.3 rows are graded with --keep-tracks as N04.3 graded them (their breaches were on boards with their own copper, and Q22.3's restore only acts there); pocketsdr-v3-0 and fc-rom are routed whole, as Q22.10 and Q22.12 graded them and as their limits were measured

grading: one KiCad grade per distinct session: each arm and row is one grade.sh call, which routes once and grades that session once (kicad-cli pcb drc --severity-all --refill-zones of the unrouted and the routed board, each with the row's original .kicad_pro/.kicad_dru and the copper classes forced to error; summary `rules` = project on every row); nothing is graded twice or rerun. The arms' sessions come from different DSNs and are imported by different plugins, so each grade is its own; two byte-identical sessions of a row are reported as such. Then via_in_pad.py (the q22 commit's) on OUT/ARM/ROW/routed/BASE.kicad_pcb and OUT/ARM/ROW/unrouted/BASE.kicad_pcb with KiCad's python3. Row by row in set order, before first, then q22; one route and one kicad-cli at a time (start a grade.sh call only while `pgrep -x kicad-cli` shows none)
limits: every route under ulimit -v 8000000 and timeout -k 10 LIMIT, LIMIT = the row's timeout_s, the same in both arms (decided 2026-10-20): 300 s for every row but canary-pwr (600 s); fc-rom also gets the router's own --timeout 270 after the plugin's flags (ROW_ARGS). Sources per row in boards.rows.*.limit_source. A route stopped by its limit is aborted = 1; it is graded when it left a SES (the CLI saves on SIGTERM and at its own --timeout), its guard counts like any other row's, and it is not rerun. A row with no SES is not graded (summary graded false) and is unjudged. Routing time in the worst case: 2 x (13 x 300 + 600) s = 2.5 h; Q22.8 is a batch measurement and goes through the orchestrator's heavy-run queue

metric_definitions.via_in_pad: via_in_pad.py's vias_in_pads on the routed board minus the input (unrouted) board's, floored at 0; the gate requires it as a hard metric (D8: a via in a pad is a failure)
metric_definitions.below_minimum: routed tracks and vias, those whose nanometre copper key (oracle_lib.copper_key over oracle_lib.read_copper of OUT/ARM/ROW/routed/BASE.kicad_pcb) the input board (OUT/ARM/ROW/unrouted/BASE.kicad_pcb, oracle_lib.input_copper_keys) does not have, strictly below the Board Setup minimum track width, via diameter or via drill (OUT/ARM/ROW/routed/copper.json board_minimums_mm), summed: the copper basis of Q22.2, computed as tools/kicad-reader/plugin-input-ab.sh's below_minimum does
metric_definitions.manufacturing_breaches: the sum over clearance, hole_clearance, hole_to_hole, copper_edge_clearance, track_width, via_diameter, annular_width, drill_out_of_range, solder_mask_bridge, shorting_items of summary drc_real_by_type: the routing-caused KiCad DRC items on the copper basis (summary routing_caused_basis = copper; Q22.2: an item is routing-caused when it involves a track or via the input board does not have at the same nanometre coordinates, width, layer and net). A row whose summary says routing_caused_basis = report is unjudged
metric_definitions.kicad_unconnected: summary unconnected_items: kicad-cli's unconnected items on the routed board
metric_definitions.errors_by_type: summary routed_by_type: every DRC item on the routed board by type, pre-existing ones included
metric_definitions.drc_real: summary drc_real, the sum of routing_caused_by_type
metric_definitions.input_unconnected: summary input_unconnected_items: kicad-cli's unconnected items on the unrouted board (the input as given for keep_tracks rows, the stripped board otherwise)
metric_definitions.route_seconds: summary engine_seconds: the engine command's wall time
metric_definitions.aborted: 1 when summary engine_exit >= 124 (timeout's kill) or OUT/ARM/ROW/work/engine.log has 'finished with state: TIMED_OUT' (the router's own --timeout); else 0
metric_definitions.below_minimum_all: the sum of summary copper.below_minimum (kicad_steps.py stats): every track and via on the routed board below the Board Setup minimums, input copper included; reported only, since keep_tracks rows carry the designer's own copper
metric_definitions.via_in_pad_raw: via_in_pad.py's vias_in_pads on the routed board

guards: Absolute, decided 2026-10-20 (routing-quality.md, order of importance item 1): in q22, on every row, manufacturing_breaches = 0 (routing-caused clearance, hole_clearance, hole_to_hole, copper_edge_clearance, track_width, via_diameter, annular_width, drill_out_of_range, solder_mask_bridge, shorting_items) and below_minimum = 0, on the copper basis (Q22.2); and via_in_pad = 0, the hard metric the gate requires (D8). Not 'no new breach versus before'. before is reported, not guarded: its breaches are the point
keep_rule: Decided 2026-10-20: Q22's fixes are correctness fixes, already landed, so there is no profile promotion. The verdict is 'guards met' when every row's q22 arm is graded on the copper basis with manufacturing_breaches = 0, below_minimum = 0 and via_in_pad = 0. Otherwise it is 'guards not met', with each row and item that breaks them (DRC type, the items KiCad names, the rule and the actual distance). A q22 row that is not graded is unjudged, and the verdict is then 'not established on the full set', with the unjudged rows named. A guard breach is a new Q22 item to fix, not a reason to remove a fix (decided 2026-10-20)
keep_rule_by_hand: The gate expresses the zero guards (hard metrics on the verdict pair's candidate) but not 'no keep decision', so Q22.8 applies the rule from the records: (1) records.json carries per row and arm the metrics above from OUT/ARM/ROW/summary.json, via_in_pad.json and the copper computation, the input sha256 and the arms block as registered; (2) `freerouting-dev gate --records records.json --baseline baseline.json --prereg docs/roadmap/prereg/Q22.json --write-baseline`, then `freerouting-dev gate --records records.json --prereg docs/roadmap/prereg/Q22.json --all-pairs`; both must report 0 refusals; (3) the verdict comes from the verdict pair's HARD and UNGRADED lines only: none gives 'guards met'; every HARD line names a row and metric that breaks a guard; every UNGRADED line is an unjudged row; (4) the paired improve/regress verdict on kicad_unconnected and the reported pair's HARD lines (before's breaches) are printed and do not decide anything
report: per row and arm: kicad_unconnected and input_unconnected; routing_caused_by_type (every type) and manufacturing_breaches, below_minimum, via_in_pad; route_seconds and aborted; the session sha256 (OUT/ARM/ROW/work/BASE.ses) and whether the row's two sessions are byte-identical; per row the change in kicad_unconnected (q22 - before). Q22.8's note names the rows whose kicad_unconnected the obstacles of Q22.4 cost (Q22.8's Accept clause), with the export log's counts of copper-graphic keepouts and net-shape areas for each
known_effects: before's plugin writes no copper-graphic keepouts, passes no --kicad-dru, board minimum clearance or hole-to-hole minimum, and its import does not restore input copper, so its rows are expected to carry the breaches Q22 fixed. The q22 arm's extra obstacles and floors can leave connections open (Q22.4, Q22.14/Q22.15: ch32v003 18 -> 34 KiCad unconnected); that cost is reported, not judged (Q22 'Decisions made here'). A route cut by its limit stops at a wall-clock point ('result is timing-dependent' in the router log), so an aborted row's numbers are not reproducible to the item; the guard holds for whatever it wrote
stop_rule: one registered run per arm and row; no reruns with other settings; an aborted route is graded if it left a SES and is not rerun. A change after the first number goes in `amendments` with its reason
seen_before_registration: Numbers on these rows exist only from other setups, none with these two arms under this grader: N04.3's center arm (main b98074e, bare export, --keep-tracks; the breach table at the top of Q22); Q22.2's and Q22.3's re-summaries and re-imports of those saved sessions; Q22.4's re-measure (pcietest clearance 130 -> 0 at a 120 s cut, sonde-xilinx 2 -> 0, mydevboard 0 -> 0; vfo, miniscope and openair, not rows here); Q22.6's canary-pwr (inside_pad, 0 clearance, 58 unconnected, 227 s); Q22.10's pocketsdr-v3-0 (clearance 499 -> 0, 39 unconnected at 217.8 s); Q22.11's ch32v003 and pocketsdr-v3-0; Q22.12's fc-rom (solder_mask_bridge 7, 79 unconnected, 271-273 s); Q22.14/Q22.15's ch32v003 (34 unconnected, 0 breaches at a36a5c0). The registration was written from those notes; nothing was routed or graded for it
not_registered: profile legacy, and any plugin option off its default
the bare export (grade.sh without --export plugin) and the kicad_pcb board input (K13's measurement)
uncapped or longer routes of the rows cut by their limit
Windows KiCad 10.0.5, and running inside the KiCad editor
tidiness (FREEROUTING_DEV is off in both arms)
Q22.7's first wording of the arms ('before (main)' and 'q22 (Q22.2-Q22.6)'), replaced on 2026-10-20 by a8b4ae7 and the q22 commit
